subcategory: §0 CONTRACT GROUP — WHICH RULE SET APPLIES
rule_text: Cancellation procedures differ depending on the customer's contract start date. Before applying any rule in this document, the AI must first determine which group the customer belongs to. Groups are named by date range, not by letter, so there is no risk of mixing them up.

Section 18 rules apply to this group. Sections 3 and 6 (the standard SIM deposit and Wi-Fi deposit rules) do NOT apply to Previous contracts — Section 18 replaces them.
All other sections of this document (1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12–17, 19) apply as written.

subcategory: §0.2 CURRENT CONTRACTS — Started December 11, 2024 or Later
rule_text:
Sections 3 and 6 apply exactly as written for this group — the ¥800 SIM deposit refunded as a bill discount (Section 3), and the Wi-Fi deposit rules including the restriction against using it for unpaid bills or other charges (Section 6). Section 18 does NOT apply to Current contracts.
All other sections of this document (1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12–17, 19) apply as written.

The AI must ask for or confirm the customer's contract start date before applying Sections 3/6 vs. Section 18. Contract start date is an account-based fact (see Section 16.2) — the AI may ask the customer what it is, but must treat it as unconfirmed until verified by support, the same as usage period or payment coverage.
Quick reference:
- Contract started before December 11, 2024 → PREVIOUS → Section 18 applies.
- Contract started December 11, 2024 or later → CURRENT → Sections 3 and 6 apply as written.

For both SIM Card and Wi-Fi services, the standard payment covers:
- 3 consecutive months of service usage.
- The applicable COD (Cash on Delivery) price.
A single payment record in the system may therefore represent payment for 3 consecutive months of service plus the COD price.
When checking a customer's payment status, the AI must understand that one payment record can cover 3 consecutive months.
The AI must check the payment dates and payment coverage before determining whether the customer has an unpaid bill.
The AI must NOT assume that a customer has an unpaid bill simply because there is only one payment record for multiple months.
If the payment coverage cannot be confirmed from the available information, the AI must not guess. The case should be verified by the support team.

rule_text:
The minimum usage period for a SIM Card is 4 months.
If a customer cancels the SIM Card before completing 4 months of usage:
- A ¥5,000 cancellation fee applies.
- The customer must pay all unpaid bills.
If a customer has completed 4 months or more of usage:
- The ¥5,000 cancellation fee does not apply.
- The customer must still pay all unpaid bills.

If the SIM Card status is "Re-issue" (Terminated):
- The customer must pay the applicable re-issue (terminated) fee.
- The customer must pay all unpaid bills.
- The ¥5,000 cancellation fee does not apply.
The Re-issue (Terminated) rule takes priority over the normal ¥5,000 cancellation-fee rule.

subcategory: §3 SIM CARD CANCELLATION NOTICE PERIOD (CURRENT CONTRACTS — Dec 11, 2024 or later)
rule_text: The cancellation notice period determines whether the ¥800 deposit can be refunded. This section applies to CURRENT contracts only. For PREVIOUS contracts (before Dec 11, 2024), see Section 18 instead.

subcategory: §3.1 Two Months or More Advance Notice
rule_text:
If the customer provides 2 months or more advance notice:
- The ¥800 deposit will be refunded.
- The ¥800 deposit will be refunded as a discount on the customer's next bill.
- The ¥800 deposit is not refunded as cash.

If the customer provides 1 month advance notice:
- The ¥800 deposit may be refunded.
- The refund will be provided as a discount on the customer's next bill.
- Approval is required.
The AI must not tell the customer that the ¥800 refund is approved until approval has been confirmed.

subcategory: §3.3 Less Than One Month Advance Notice
rule_text:
If the customer provides less than 1 month advance notice:
- The request is considered an urgent cancellation.
- The ¥800 deposit will not be refunded.
- The customer must return the SIM Card.

The minimum usage period for Wi-Fi is 4 months.
If a customer cancels the Wi-Fi service before completing 4 months of usage:
- A ¥5,000 cancellation fee applies.
- The customer must pay all unpaid bills.
- The Wi-Fi device and SIM Card must be returned.
If a customer has completed 4 months or more of usage:
- The ¥5,000 cancellation fee does not apply.
- The customer must still pay all unpaid bills.
- The Wi-Fi device and SIM Card must be returned.

If the Wi-Fi status is "Re-issue" (Terminated):
- The customer must pay the applicable re-issue (terminated) fee.
- The customer must pay all unpaid bills.
- The ¥5,000 cancellation fee does not apply.
- The Wi-Fi device and SIM Card must be returned.
The Re-issue (Terminated) rule takes priority over the normal ¥5,000 cancellation-fee rule.

rule_text:
5. The cancellation process is completed after the returned Wi-Fi device and SIM Card have been received and confirmed by the office.
The AI must remind the customer that BOTH the Wi-Fi device AND the SIM Card must be returned.
This process applies to both PREVIOUS and CURRENT contracts.

subcategory: §6 WI-FI DEPOSIT REFUND (CURRENT CONTRACTS — Dec 11, 2024 or later)
rule_text:
The Wi-Fi deposit refund follows these rules. This section applies to CURRENT contracts only. For PREVIOUS contracts (before Dec 11, 2024), see Section 18 instead — the rule against using the deposit for unpaid bills or other charges does NOT apply to Previous contracts.
- The customer may request the deposit refund after the returned Wi-Fi device and SIM Card have been received by the office.
- The deposit refund is processed by bank transfer.
- The customer can request the deposit refund within 60 days after the cancellation request.
- The deposit refund cannot be used as payment for unpaid bills.
- The deposit refund cannot be used as payment for damage fees.
- The deposit refund cannot be used as payment for lost-device fees or lost-item fees.

Before telling a customer that they have an unpaid bill, the AI must verify the customer's payment coverage.
Because the standard payment covers 3 consecutive months of service plus the COD price:
- One payment record may cover 3 consecutive months.
- The AI must not treat each month as requiring a separate payment record.
- The AI must check the payment date and the months covered by the payment.
- Only confirmed unpaid amounts should be described as unpaid bills.
If the AI cannot determine which months are covered by a payment:
- Do not guess.
- Do not tell the customer that they owe money.
- Request verification from the support team.

The AI must use the rules in this document as the authoritative source for SIM Card and Wi-Fi cancellation questions.
The AI must:
- Follow the cancellation rules exactly.
- Never invent a fee.
- Never invent a refund.
- Never waive a fee unless the rules explicitly allow it.
- Never promise an approval that has not been confirmed.
- Never assume a payment is missing without checking its coverage.
- Never assume that one payment record represents only one month.
- Never remove unpaid bills from the customer's responsibility.
- Never tell a customer that a deposit can be used to pay an amount when the rules prohibit it for their contract group (deposits CAN be used for unpaid bills/other charges for LEGACY contracts only — see Section 18.3 — and CANNOT for Current contracts — see Section 6).
- Never state or guess a deposit amount that is not explicitly given in this document (see Section 18.2 for Legacy contracts).
- Never apply Section 3/6 (Current-contract rules) to a Legacy contract, or Section 18 (Legacy-contract rules) to a Current contract.
- Ask for missing information when necessary.
- Escalate cases that cannot be determined from the available information.

subcategory: §12 EXAMPLE: SIM CARD CANCELLATION BEFORE 4 MONTHS
rule_text:
If a customer has used a SIM Card for less than 4 months and requests cancellation:
- The customer has not completed the minimum 4-month usage period.
- A ¥5,000 cancellation fee applies.
- The customer must pay any confirmed unpaid bills.
- The AI must verify payment coverage before identifying unpaid bills.
- The applicable deposit rule depends on the cancellation notice period and the customer's contract group (see Sections 3 and 18).
If notice is 2 months or more:
- CURRENT contracts: the ¥800 deposit is refunded as a discount on the next bill (Section 3.1).
- PREVIOUS contracts: the deposit is refunded by bank transfer, at the Previous amount (see Section 18.2).
If notice is exactly 1 month:
- The deposit may be refunded, using the refund method for the customer's contract group.
- Approval is required.
If notice is less than 1 month:
- The cancellation is considered urgent.
- The deposit is not refunded.
- The SIM Card must be returned.

subcategory: §13 EXAMPLE: SIM CARD CANCELLATION AFTER 4 MONTHS
rule_text:
If a customer has completed 4 months or more of SIM Card usage:
- The ¥5,000 cancellation fee does not apply.
- The customer must pay all confirmed unpaid bills.
- The AI must verify payment coverage before identifying unpaid bills.
- The applicable deposit rule depends on the cancellation notice period and the customer's contract group (see Sections 3 and 18).

If the customer's service status is "Re-issue" (Terminated):
- The applicable re-issue (Terminated) fee applies.
- All confirmed unpaid bills must be paid.
- The ¥5,000 cancellation fee does not apply.
This rule applies regardless of whether the customer has used the service for less than or more than 4 months, and regardless of contract group.

When a customer requests Wi-Fi cancellation:
- The Wi-Fi device must be returned.
- The SIM Card must be returned.
- A photo must be provided as proof of return.
- The returned Wi-Fi device and SIM Card must be received by the office.
- The cancellation is completed after the returned equipment is received and confirmed.
- The deposit refund can be requested after the returned equipment has been received.
- The deposit refund is processed by bank transfer.
- The deposit refund request must be made within 60 days after the cancellation request.
- CURRENT contracts: the deposit cannot be used to pay unpaid bills, damage fees, or lost-device/lost-item fees (Section 6).
- PREVIOUS contracts: the deposit CAN be used to pay unpaid bills or other charges (see Section 18.3).

subcategory: §16 WHAT THE AI CAN CALCULATE VS. WHAT REQUIRES VERIFICATION
rule_text: No customer account database is connected to the AI. The AI does not have independent access to payment records, usage history, or account status. This means the AI must clearly separate two types of information:

The AI may calculate the following directly from dates provided by the customer or the system, since this is arithmetic and does not require account data:
- The cancellation notice period, based on the date the cancellation request is submitted and the requested effective cancellation date.
- Which of the 3 notice-period tiers applies (2 months or more / 1 month / less than 1 month).
- The corresponding deposit refund rule that applies to that tier, as stated in Section 3 (Current contracts) or Section 18 (Previous contracts).
The AI may state this calculated result to the customer directly. This is not a guess and does not require escalation.

subcategory: §16.2 Account-Based Facts (AI must not confirm — requires support verification)
rule_text:
The AI must NOT confirm, calculate, or state as fact any of the following based on the customer's own claims, since these require verified account/billing data that the AI does not have access to:
- Total usage period (whether 4 months or more has actually been completed).
- Payment status and payment coverage (which months a payment record actually covers).
- Confirmed unpaid bills or amounts owed.
- Re-issue (Terminated) status of the SIM Card or Wi-Fi device.
- Wi-Fi device or SIM Card return/receipt status.
- Approval status for a 1-month-notice deposit refund.
- Contract start date / contract group (Previous vs. Current).
For all of the above, the AI may explain which rule would apply if a given fact is confirmed (e.g., "if your usage is confirmed at 4 months or more, the ¥5,000 fee would not apply"), but must frame it conditionally and state that final confirmation comes from the support team. The AI must not tell the customer a fee is waived, a bill is unpaid, or a refund is approved based solely on the customer's own statement.
17. [Reserved — not used. See Section 19 for undefined/unclear cases.]

subcategory: §18 PREVIOUS CONTRACT RULES — CONTRACTS STARTED BEFORE DECEMBER 11, 2024
rule_text: This section applies ONLY to customers whose contract started before December 11, 2024 (PREVIOUS contracts). For these customers, this section REPLACES Sections 3 and 6. All other sections of this document still apply unchanged to this group.

Unlike Current contracts, Previous customers must return the SIM card on cancellation, with Re-Issue (Terminated) status in addition to the Wi-Fi device where applicable.
- SIM Card cancellation: the SIM card must be returned.
- Wi-Fi cancellation: both the Wi-Fi device and the SIM card must be returned (same as Section 5).
- The AI must remind Previous customers that the SIM card must be returned even for a SIM-card-only cancellation, which is a change from Current contracts, where SIM card return is only explicitly required in the "less than 1 month notice" case (Section 3.3).

subcategory: §18.2 SIM Card Deposit Amount and Refund Method (Previous)
rule_text:
- The SIM card deposit amount for Previous contracts differs from the ¥800 deposit used for Current contracts. The exact amount is not defined in this document.
- The AI must NOT state, guess, or estimate the Previous SIM card deposit amount under any circumstances. If a customer asks how much their deposit is, the AI must tell them the amount will be confirmed by the support team and must not offer a figure, including the ¥800 Current-contract amount.
- The AI may still tell a Previous customer that their deposit refund follows a different amount and process than Current contracts, without stating the number.
- The SIM card deposit is refunded by bank transfer, not as a discount on the next bill (this differs from Section 3, where the Current-contract ¥800 deposit is only ever refunded as a bill discount, never as cash or bank transfer).
- The notice-period tiers themselves (2 months or more / 1 month / less than 1 month) still determine refund eligibility the same way as Section 3.1–3.3, unless and until a different notice-period rule is confirmed for Previous contracts. Only the deposit amount and refund method change.

subcategory: §18.3 Deposit Use for Unpaid Bills and Other Charges (Previous)
rule_text:
This is a direct reversal of the Current-contract rule in Section 6:
- For Previous contracts, both the SIM card deposit and the Wi-Fi device deposit CAN be used as payment for unpaid bills or other charges.
- This differs from Current contracts (Section 6), where the Wi-Fi deposit explicitly CANNOT be used for unpaid bills, damage fees, or lost-device/lost-item fees.
- The AI must not apply the Section 6 restriction to Previous customers.
- The AI should still confirm with support before actually netting a deposit against a specific unpaid bill or charge, since the exact amount of the unpaid bill/charge remains an account-based fact under Section 16.2.

subcategory: §18.4 Summary of Differences: Previous vs. Current
rule_text:
- SIM card return: required for Previous (all cancellations); only explicitly required for Current contracts in the less-than-1-month notice case.
- SIM card deposit amount: different from ¥800 for Previous; exact amount not defined here — the AI must never state or guess it and must refer the customer to support.
- SIM card deposit refund method: bank transfer for Previous; bill discount only for Current.
- Deposit usage for unpaid bills/charges: allowed for Previous (both SIM and Wi-Fi deposits); not allowed for Current contracts (Wi-Fi deposit, per Section 6).
- All other rules (minimum usage period, ¥5,000 cancellation fee, re-issue (termination) fee priority, Wi-Fi return process, 60-day refund request window) are unchanged between groups unless stated otherwise above.

If a customer's situation does not clearly match these rules:
- The AI must not guess.
- The AI must not create a new rule.
- The AI must not create a new fee.
- The AI must not promise a refund.
- The AI must ask for the missing information or escalate the case to human support.
The information in this document is the authoritative cancellation policy for SIM Card and Wi-Fi services.

Replacement, and Cancellation. It does not cover cancellation fees or notice-period

category: CS AI DOC: AI_ Returning of SIMDevice
rule_text:
Regardless of any return waiver described in this document (see Section 3.1), the
customer's account must have no unpaid bills. This requirement applies universally —
to Change Plan, Replacement, and Cancellation alike. A return waiver only affects
whether physical items must be returned; it never waives the no-unpaid-bills
requirement.
No customer account database is connected to the AI (see Section 7). The AI must not
confirm or deny unpaid-bill status based on the customer's own claim — this must be
verified by the support team, the same as in the Cancellation Rules document.

category: CS AI DOC: AI_ Returning of SIMDevice
rule_text:
Returning of the SIM card and/or Wi-Fi device is required whenever a customer changes
plan or receives a replacement. Return whichever item corresponds to what was changed
or replaced — SIM card, Wi-Fi device, or both.

category: CS AI DOC: AI_ Returning of SIMDevice
rule_text:
The return must be completed within 7 days after the customer receives the new SIM
card. This applies to all Change Plan and Replacement returns, for both SIM card and
Wi-Fi plan.
If the return is not completed within 7 days, the customer will receive a letter
regarding the non-returned item, and will be penalized.
The exact penalty amount is intentionally not disclosed to customers. The AI may
confirm that a penalty applies and that a letter will be sent, but must never state or
guess a specific figure — this is a non-disclosure policy, not a missing fact, so there
is nothing to escalate for; the answer is simply that the amount isn't shared.

category: CS AI DOC: AI_ Returning of SIMDevice
rule_text:
A SIM card issued for a change plan or a replacement is issued with a new MSN (phone
number). The customer cannot retain their previous number. This applies to both Change
Plan and Replacement cases.

category: CS AI DOC: AI_ Returning of SIMDevice
rule_text:
CURRENT contracts (started December 11, 2024 or later):
- 2 months or more advance notice: SIM card return is NOT required. Payment card
return is NOT required either — both are waived together.
- Exactly 1 month advance notice: SIM card return is NOT required. Payment card return
is NOT required — both are waived together, same as the 2-month tier.
- Less than 1 month advance notice (urgent cancellation): the SIM card MUST be
returned. The payment card MUST be returned. If the return is not completed by the
requested cancellation date, billing continues and the contract is treated as NOT
cancelled — the cancellation does not take effect until the return is completed.
- In every case, no unpaid bills is still required (see Section 1) — this is never
waived, even when the SIM/payment card return is waived.
PREVIOUS contracts (started before December 11, 2024):
- The SIM card must be returned, regardless of notice period and status (Active/IN USE, RE-ISSUE (Terminated). There is no notice-period
waiver for Previous contracts.
- The return deadline is the end of the calendar month in which the cancellation takes
effect (not the month the request was submitted, if different).
- The customer must pay the bill for the month in which cancellation takes effect.
- If the SIM card, device (if applicable), payment card, and accessories are not
returned by the end of that month, the customer will be charged for the following
month's bill as well. This is the specific consequence of a late Previous return.
- Example: a customer messages on August 10 requesting cancellation effective end of August

This end-of-month deadline and next-month-billing consequence applies to PREVIOUS

less-than-1-month-notice tier, the consequence is different: the ¥800 deposit is

requested cancellation date, billing continues and the contract is treated as NOT

following month" rule. Do not apply the Legacy end-of-month framing to Current
contracts, or vice versa.

category: CS AI DOC: AI_ Returning of SIMDevice
rule_text:
Wi-Fi plan cancellation always requires returning ALL of the following, regardless of
notice period and regardless of Previous vs. Current contract group:
- The Wi-Fi device.
- The SIM card.
- All accessories included with the original order (e.g. charger, adapter, dock,
cable).
- The payment card.
Confirmed: there is no notice-period or Previous/Current waiver for Wi-Fi cancellation
returns — unlike SIM Card Plan cancellation, notice period has no effect on what must

customer what to return for a Wi-Fi cancellation — bringing it up is unnecessary and

It applies ONLY to refunds paid by bank transfer. It does NOT apply to the Current

submit bank details for in that case, since it's applied automatically.
This document should be read together with:
- The Cancellation Rules document (AI_Cancellation) for
which deposit amount and refund method applies to a given contract group and notice
period.
- The Returning Rules document (AI_ Returning of SIM/Device) for what must be
physically returned before a deposit refund can be requested or processed.

This bank-transfer refund process applies to:
- PREVIOUS contracts (before December 11, 2024): both SIM Card Plan and Wi-Fi Plan
deposits (see Cancellation Rules Section 18.2).
- CURRENT contracts (December 11, 2024 or later): Wi-Fi Plan deposits only (see
Cancellation Rules Section 6). It does NOT apply to Current SIM Card Plan deposits
(bill discount only — see Section 0 above).

Deposit refunds under this topic are paid ONLY by bank transfer. No cash or in-person
refund is available. (This is separate from the Current SIM Plan bill-discount method,
which is out of scope for this document — see Section 0.)
Acceptable receiving banks:
- A bank within Japan, OR
- A bank in the customer's home country, for customers who have already returned home.

- Picture of the bank account book or cash card.
- Account number.
- Account holder's name.
- Name of the bank, or bank code.
- Name of the branch, or branch code.

- Destination/country.
- Delivery method: bank transfer.
- Bank name.
- Branch code or name.
- Account number.
- Account name.
- Nationality.
- Postal code.
- Branch address.
- Mobile phone number.
- Branch landline phone number.
- Personal email address.
- Email language.
[SECURITY NOTE: these are sensitive personal and financial details. The AI may mention
which categories of information are required to claim the refund (e.g., account
number, account holder's name, bank/branch details), but must not collect these
details directly as plain chat text. If the customer wants to proceed, the AI should
hand off to the support team, who handle actual collection and submission of these
details.]

subcategory: §4.1 When the Customer Can Request the Refund
rule_text:
The customer may submit the deposit refund request (including bank details) as soon as
they have sent proof of return. This is the earliest point the request can be made.

subcategory: §4.2 When the Request Is Actually Processed
rule_text:
Customer support processes the request for approval only after the returned rental
item has been received and confirmed by the office. Submitting the request early (at
proof-of-return stage) does not skip this step — it only means the paperwork is ready
in advance; approval still waits for physical confirmation of the return.

Once the returned rental item has been received and verified in the office, deposit
refund processing takes 8–14 days.

A deposit slip is sent to the customer once the deposit refund has been credited to the
submitted bank account.
5. 60-DAY CLAIM PERIOD
There is a 60-day deposit claim period from the effective date of the cancellation
(not the date the cancellation request was submitted). If the deposit refund is not
claimed within this window, it cannot be processed and is forfeited.

subcategory: §6 PREVIOUS CONTRACTS — DEPOSIT AS PAYMENT (SIM Card Plan and Wi-Fi Plan)
rule_text:
This reflects the Legacy rule already established in the Cancellation Rules document
(Section 18.3): for Previous contracts, the deposit CAN be used as payment.
- The deposit can be applied as payment toward unpaid bills or other charges (this
includes damage-related charges, since Legacy contracts allow the deposit to be used
as payment generally, not just for a specific bill type).
- If a remaining amount is left over after such charges are covered, that remaining
amount is refunded by bank transfer.
- If the deposit amount is not enough to cover the unpaid bills or other charges, the
customer must pay the remaining (lacking) amount through their registered payment
method.
- Returning of rental items still applies for Previous contracts — see the Returning
Rules document before processing any deposit refund; the return requirement is a
separate condition from how the deposit is applied.

subcategory: §7 CURRENT CONTRACTS — WI-FI PLAN DEPOSIT REFUND
rule_text:
This reflects the Current-contract rule already established in the Cancellation Rules
document (Section 6): the deposit CANNOT be used as payment for anything.
- The deposit cannot be used as payment for unpaid bills, damage fees, or any other
charge. If there is a separate unpaid bill or damage fee, it is billed separately
through the customer's registered payment method — the deposit is never applied
toward it.
- The refund is solely by bank transfer (see Section 2).
- Even though the deposit cannot be used as payment, the refund itself CAN still be
withheld entirely (not paid out) if there are unresolved issues such as:
- The device is found damaged upon receipt at the office.
- There are unpaid bills on the account.
This is a forfeiture of the refund, not an application of the deposit as payment —
the distinction matters: the deposit money is never credited against the damage fee
or unpaid bill invoice, but the customer may still not receive it back if these
issues are present.
- Not all requested deposit refunds are confirmed or approved — a damaged device or
unpaid bills are example reasons a refund cannot be processed.

subcategory: §8 WHAT THE AI CAN CALCULATE VS. WHAT REQUIRES VERIFICATION
rule_text:
No customer account database is connected to the AI. The AI does not have independent
access to return-receipt confirmation, damage assessments, or payment records.

- Whether the customer is still within the 60-day claim period, based on the
cancellation's effective date (not the request submission date).
- An estimated refund completion window (8–14 days), once the customer confirms the
office has already received and verified the returned item — but the AI must not
claim the office HAS received/verified the item; that must come from the customer or
be confirmed by support.

subcategory: §8.2 Account-Based Facts (AI must not confirm — requires support verification)
rule_text:
- Whether the returned item has actually been received and verified by the office.
- Whether the device was found damaged upon receipt.
- Whether there are unpaid bills on the account.
- Whether a refund request has been approved.
- The customer's contract group (Previous vs. Current) and, for Legacy, the exact amount
remaining after any unpaid bills/charges are applied.
For all of the above, the AI may explain what WOULD happen if a given fact is
confirmed, but must frame it conditionally and state that final confirmation and
approval come from the support team.

- Never state or confirm that a specific refund amount will be paid — the Legacy
"remaining amount after offsets" and any Current-contract withholding decision are
account-based facts requiring support confirmation.
- Never imply that submitting bank details early (Section 4.1) guarantees approval —
approval still depends on office confirmation of the physical return and account
status.
- Never state that a Current-contract deposit can be used as payment for anything — it
cannot, under any circumstance.
- Never guess at what counts as "damage" or how much a damage fee will be — refer to
support.
- Do not collect full bank account numbers or other sensitive financial/personal
details as plain chat text. The AI may mention which categories of information are
needed to claim the refund; if the customer wants to proceed, hand off to the
support team, who handle actual collection and submission of those details.
- Always confirm the customer's contract group and which service (SIM or Wi-Fi) before
explaining refund method or timing, since Current SIM Plan refunds are out of scope
for this topic entirely (see Section 0).
- Escalate cases that cannot be determined from the available information.

If a customer's situation does not clearly match these rules:
- The AI must not guess.
- The AI must not create a new rule, timeframe, or refund amount.
- The AI must ask for the missing information or escalate the case to human support.
The information in this document is the authoritative deposit refund policy, to be read
together with the Cancellation Rules and Returning Rules documents.

subcategory: §0 TOPIC SCOPE AND RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER TOPICS
rule_text:
This document covers Change Plan and Replacement fees, eligibility, payment method, and
billing timing. It does NOT cover what must be physically returned or how — for that,
see the Returning of SIM/Device document (AI_ Returning of SIM/Device), which already
covers the 7-day return deadline, the new-phone-number (MSN) rule, and the "don't
return the payment card" rule for Change Plan/Replacement. Both documents must be read
together for a complete answer.
Change Plan applies to BOTH Previous (before Dec 11, 2024) and Current (Dec 11, 2024 or
later) contracts — there is no contract-group-based fee difference for Change Plan or
Replacement, unlike Cancellation.
Replacement due to damage or loss keeps the customer's CURRENT plan — it is not a plan
change, only a physical item replacement.
[NAMING NOTE: this document has its own "within 7 days" rule (Section 6) that is
DIFFERENT from the Returning Rules document's 7-day return deadline (Section 2.2 of
that document). Section 6 here is about handling a  change plan and replacement request
shortly after a previous delivery — not about returning an old item. Do not conflate
the two when answering a customer.]

subcategory: §1 GENERAL RULES THAT APPLY TO EVERY CHANGE PLAN CASE
rule_text:
The following apply to all Change Plan scenarios in Sections 2–5, unless stated
otherwise:
- The change plan fee does NOT include the customer's regular bill payment — billing
for the current plan continues separately and is not replaced by the change fee.
- There must be no unpaid bills on the account for the customer to be eligible for a
change plan.
- The current month's bill must be paid.
- The change plan fee is a separate, one-time charge, paid via Cash on Delivery (COD)
at the time the new SIM card/device is delivered — it is not billed through the
customer's registered payment method.
- The new plan's monthly fee starts being billed starting the FOLLOWING month,
regardless of whether the change was made before or after the billing due date —
EXCEPT when the change's effective date is the 1st of the month, in which case the
new monthly fee applies immediately, starting that same month's bill. (Example: a
change effective December 1st means the December bill is already at the new plan's
rate.)
- The change plan fee itself (whether flat or based on the new plan's monthly amount)
is a SEPARATE, one-time charge from the ongoing monthly billing described above — the
customer is not exempt from the following month's regular bill at the new rate just
because they paid a change fee that happened to be calculated using that same monthly
amount.
- A new SIM card (and/or device, depending on scenario) with a new phone number (MSN)
will be sent, and the old SIM card (and/or device) must be returned — see the
Returning Rules document for the full return requirements.

2.1 Fee
- Effective date = 1st of the month: fee is ¥2,500 (flat).
- Effective date = middle of the month: fee is the new plan's monthly fee + ¥700
shipping fee. State this as the formula — "your new plan's monthly fee plus ¥700
shipping" — rather than an actual number. Not knowing the exact plan price is fine;
stating the formula is a complete, correct answer and does not need escalation.

Follows Section 1's general rules (no unpaid bills, COD payment, billing timing, new
SIM with new number sent, old SIM must be returned).

subcategory: §3 SIM PLAN / WI-FI PLAN → WI-FI PLAN
rule_text:
3.1 Fee
- Effective date = 1st of the month: fee is ¥2,500 + ¥2,000 (Wi-Fi device rental fee) =
¥4,500 total.
- Effective date = middle of the month: fee is the new plan's monthly fee + ¥2,000
(Wi-Fi device rental fee) + ¥700 shipping fee. State this as the formula, the same | ¥3,300 + Shipping ¥700
way as Section 2.1 — an exact number isn't needed for a complete answer.
- The ¥2,000 Wi-Fi device rental fee here is a ONE-TIME charge only, paid via COD at
the time of change. There is no separate ongoing monthly device rental charge
afterward.

Follows Section 1's general rules. A new SIM card AND device (with new number) will be
sent; the old SIM card and/or device must be returned.

subcategory: §4 ADDING POCKET WI-FI ONLY (NO NEW SIM CARD SENT)
rule_text:
- Applies when a customer on an existing SIM plan wants to add a pocket Wi-Fi device
without changing or replacing their SIM card.
- Fee is ¥2,000 only, paid via COD, one-time.
- This is described in the source information as usually applying to Softbank plans
and devices such as JT101, W06, WX04, W05. [This "usually" is a hedge in the source
information, not a definitive restriction — if a customer's plan/carrier or device
isn't one of these, don't assume the ¥2,000 fee still applies or that it's still
available; confirm or escalate instead.]
- The delivery date can be any date — unlike Sections 2 and 3, this fee does NOT change
based on 1st-of-month vs. mid-month timing.
- No new SIM card is sent in this scenario — only the added Wi-Fi device.

subcategory: §5.1 Upgrading Into AU5G (from SIM Plan or Wi-Fi Plan)
rule_text:
- Applies to SIM Plan or Wi-Fi Plan customers upgrading to the AU5G plan.
- Fee is ¥2,700, regardless of delivery date, in both of these cases:
- Contracted 4 months or more: ¥2,700, no additional approval needed.
- Contracted less than 4 months: ¥2,700, but requires approval before proceeding.

subcategory: §5.2 Device Upgrade Within AU5G (already on AU5G, upgrading the device)
rule_text:
- Considered a device upgrade, not a plan change.
- Fee is also ¥2,700, regardless of delivery date.
- No approval condition as Section 5.1 applies
- No new SIM card is sent in this scenario — only the upgraded AU5G Wi-Fi device.

Both 5.1 and 5.2 follow Section 1's general rules (no unpaid bills, COD payment,
billing timing, new SIM/device with new number sent, old items returned).

subcategory: §6 CHANGE PLAN / REPLACEMENT WITHIN 7 DAYS OF DELIVERY
rule_text:
If a customer requests Change Plan or Replacement within 7 days of receiving
their most recently ordered plan/device, this must be handed off to the support team to
assess the request — it is not processed through the standard flow described in
Sections 2–5. [This is a different "7 days" from the Returning Rules document's return
deadline — see the naming note in Section 0.]

- Fee is ¥3,300.
- A new SIM card with a new phone number will be sent.
- The old SIM card must be returned — return process applies (see Returning Rules
document).

subcategory: §7.2 PUK-Locked Upon Receipt (SIM Arrives Already Locked)
rule_text:
- If the SIM card is PUK-locked at the time the customer receives it (i.e., locked
before any use), this replacement is FREE of charge — the ¥3,300 fee does not apply.
- A new SIM card with a new phone number will still be sent.
- The old SIM card must still be returned — return process applies.

subcategory: §8 REPLACEMENT DUE TO DAMAGE OR LOSS
rule_text:
Before determining any fee, the AI must first ask whether the customer wants to
CONTINUE their current plan (Section 8A — a replacement is sent) or END their contract
instead (Section 8B — this becomes a cancellation). The fees, payment method, and
outcome are different between the two, so this question must come first.
8A. CONTINUING THE CURRENT PLAN
This keeps the customer's current plan — it is not a plan change.
8A.1 SIM Card Only
- Damage/loss fee is ¥4,000, which includes shipping.
- A new SIM card with a new phone number will be sent.
- Billing continues as normal (this fee does not replace or pause the regular bill).
8A.2 Device Only
Fee varies by the specific rented device:
- JT-101, 501HW, 601HW: ¥3,300 + ¥700 shipping
- JT-301: ¥6,600 + ¥700 shipping
- W04, WX04, W06: ¥2,600 + ¥700 shipping
- U3J, U3 (Cloud Air Wifi): ¥7,000 + ¥700 shipping
- X11 (NAR01), X12 (NAR03), Dock device: ¥9,160 + ¥700 shipping
- L11 (ZTR01), L12 (NAR02), L13 (ZTR02): ¥16,000 + ¥700 shipping
If the customer can identify which device they currently use, match it to this list and
state the corresponding fee. If their device is not on this list, hand off to the
support team — do not guess a fee for an unlisted device.
8A.3 Device + SIM Card Together
- Always add ¥3,300 for the SIM card portion, on top of the device fee from the table
in Section 8A.2, sent together.
- Total is: the device fee from Section 8A.2 (which already includes ¥700 shipping) +
¥3,300 for the SIM card portion. The ¥700 shipping charge is not duplicated — it's
charged once, since the device and SIM ship together in one shipment.
- If the device is not on the list in Section 8A.2, hand off to the support team.
8B. NOT CONTINUING — CONTRACT WILL END
Choosing not to continue means the contract ends — this is effectively a
damage/loss-triggered cancellation. It is governed together with the Cancellation Rules
document (cancellation_rules_and_regulations_FINAL.md), not by this document alone.
8B.1 SIM Card Only
- Damage/loss fee is ¥3,300 (no shipping charge — nothing is being shipped, since the
contract is ending).
- The standard early cancellation fee (¥5,000, per the Cancellation Rules document)
does NOT apply here, regardless of how long the customer has been contracted. Only
the ¥3,300 loss/damage fee applies — it is not combined with the ¥5,000 cancellation
fee.
- The customer must settle: any unpaid bills + the ¥3,300 loss/damage fee.
- Payable via the customer's registered payment method — NOT Cash on Delivery, since
there is no delivery in this scenario.
- Any equipment that was NOT lost or damaged, but is still in the customer's
possession (e.g., an intact Wi-Fi device on a combined plan), must still be returned
per the Returning Rules document, since the contract is ending. Only the actual
lost/damaged item is exempt from return.
- The AI must hand off to the support team to (a) report the loss/damage and (b)
process the contract cancellation — these happen together as one hand-off, not
separately.
- IMPORTANT: if the customer does not formally report the loss/damage and request
cancellation through support, the contract is NOT treated as ended, and billing
continues as normal. Simply losing or damaging the SIM does not by itself end the
contract — the customer must actively report it and choose to end the contract via
support.
8B.2 Device Only
Same fee table as Section 8A.2, but WITHOUT the ¥700 shipping fee, since nothing is
shipped when the contract ends:
- JT-101, 501HW, 601HW: ¥3,300
- JT-301: ¥6,600
- W04, WX04, W06: ¥2,600
- U3J, U3 (Cloud Air Wifi): ¥7,000
- X11 (NAR01), X12 (NAR03), Dock device: ¥9,160
- L11 (ZTR01), L12 (NAR02), L13 (ZTR02): ¥16,000
If the device is not on this list, hand off to the support team — do not guess a fee.
All the additional rules in Section 8B.1 also apply here (the ¥5,000 cancellation fee
does NOT apply — only the device loss/damage fee, unpaid bills settled via registered
payment method, non-lost/damaged equipment such as an i

Any replacement request that doesn't clearly match Sections 7 or 8 should be handed off
to the support team to assess — do not guess a fee or process for a scenario not
covered here.

subcategory: §10 WHAT THE AI CAN CALCULATE VS. WHAT REQUIRES VERIFICATION
rule_text: No customer account database is connected to the AI.

- Which fee tier applies based on effective date (1st of month vs. mid-month), once the
customer states their intended change date.
- The device-based damage/loss fee, once the customer identifies which device they
have from the Section 8A.2 or 8B.2 list (matching whether they're continuing or not).
- Whether a request falls within the Section 6 "repeat request within 7 days" window,
based on the delivery date the customer provides.

subcategory: §10.2 Account-Based Facts (AI must not confirm — requires support verification)
rule_text:
- Whether the account currently has unpaid bills (eligibility gate for all Change Plan
scenarios).
- The customer's exact contracted usage period, for the AU5G approval threshold
(Sections 5.1 and 5.2).
- Whether a device not on the Section 8A.2 or 8B.2 list qualifies, and its exact fee.
- Approval status for AU5G changes under 4 months' usage (both plan upgrades and
device-only upgrades).

- Every Change Plan and Replacement request, once the customer confirms they want to
proceed, must be handed off to the support team for actual processing — this applies
to ALL scenarios in this document, not just the specific hand-off triggers called out
in Sections 6, 8.2, and 9. The AI never itself initiates, submits, or completes a
change plan or replacement order, even for the simplest, most standard case (e.g., a
flat-fee SIM-to-SIM change on the 1st of the month). The AI's role is limited to
explaining the applicable fee, eligibility, and requirements, then handing off.
- For mid-month change fees, state the formula ("new plan's monthly fee + ¥700
shipping") rather than an actual number — this is a complete answer and does not need
escalation.
- Never guess a device's damage/loss fee if it's not on the Section 8A.2 or 8B.2 list —
hand off to support.
- Always ask whether the customer wants to CONTINUE their plan or END their contract
before quoting any damage/loss fee — the fee, payment method, and outcome differ
between the two (Section 8A vs. 8B).
- For Section 8B (not continuing), the standard ¥5,000 early cancellation fee does NOT
apply — only the loss/damage fee (Section 8B.1/8B.2/8B.3) is charged, regardless of
the customer's contracted usage period. Do not add the ¥5,000 fee on top of the
loss/damage fee for this scenario.
- Never state that a contract has ended just because a customer mentioned losing or
damaging their SIM/device — the contract only ends once the customer formally
reports it and requests cancellation through support (Section 8B.1).
- For Section 8B, remind the customer that any intact equipment (not the lost/damaged
item itself) must still be returned, since the contract is ending.
- AU5G upgrades (both upgrading into AU5G and device-only upgrades within AU5G) require
approval if the customer has been contracted or using the plan for less than 4
months — this applies to both cases equally.
- Never imply the change plan fee replaces or covers the next regular bill at the new
rate — they are separate charges (Section 1).
- Always mention that change plan fees (and the ¥2,000 device fees) are paid via Cash
on Delivery, not through the customer's registered payment method.
- Always check for a Section 6 repeat-request situation (another change/replacement
within 7 days of the last delivery) before processing a new request normally — hand
off instead if it applies.
- Escalate cases that cannot be determined from the available information.

If a customer's situation does not clearly match these rules:
- The AI must not guess.
- The AI must not create a new rule, fee, or approval outcome.
- The AI must ask for the missing information or escalate the case to human support.
The information in this document is the authoritative Change Plan and Replacement
policy, to be read together with the Returning Rules document for physical return
requirements.
